claim: OFI exposes application-facing fabric services and provider-specific implementations rather than inference or collective algorithms.
fi_tsend and fi_trecv dispatch through endpoint tagged operations while keeping payload, descriptor, peer, tag, ignore mask, and local context separate.
fi_getinfo rejects an API newer than the loaded library with ENOSYS before provider discovery.
Core getinfo skips ineligible providers, continues after provider callback failure, joins successful lists, filters/reorders, and returns ENODATA when no result remains.
ofi_register_provider validates name and mandatory fabric entrypoint, rejects provider API versions older than 1.3, and records provider type and filter visibility.
Dynamic loading uses dlopen and fi_prov_ini, then passes the returned structure through common registration.
Provider type classification distinguishes hooks, utilities, offload, LNX, and core providers; common utility helpers do not themselves mean a layered provider was selected.
ofi_layering_ok enforces exclusion/type/name rules, preserves selected two-provider ordering compatibility, and suppresses implicit layering for selected core providers.
fi_fabric resolves the top provider component, invokes its fabric callback, publishes the API version, and installs configured hooks after success.
Endpoint creation dispatches through the domain, binding through fid operations, and enablement through control with FI_ENABLE.
Input modes advertise implemented application obligations; returned modes become requirements, including asynchronous multi-IOV and context lifetime.
EFA constructs direct information before protocol-based RDM information; result order is distinct from compatibility.
Direct-attribute tests exclude TAGGED and ATOMIC, exclude send-after-send ordering, and assert automatic progress and device-dependent size limits.
Without FI_CONTEXT2, direct discovery fails for API 2.6 but succeeds at API 2.7 with all three context mode bits clear and inject size zero.
Without FI_MR_LOCAL, descriptors were ignored before API 1.22 and must be valid or NULL for newer API behavior.
Fabric child resources must be released before the fabric is closed.
Endpoint close discards outstanding operations without completions; transmission buffers remain valid until completion or returned endpoint close, and scalable contexts precede parent close.
Endpoint-associated MRs are bound/enabled explicitly and must close before the endpoint; general MR close requires the application to retire use.
The wrong-info test clears required datagram modes and observes endpoint creation ENODATA with no endpoint returned, then closes domain and fabric.
Reuse fixtures assert returned live fabric/domain pointers and names under the specific hints and capability/mode combination.
FI_AV_MAP handles are opaque, whereas FI_AV_TABLE explicitly promises first index zero and sequential insertion-order indices across insert calls; both remain scoped to the AV.
Removing an AV address invalidates its handle, leaves in-progress referencing operations undefined, and need not stop receiving peer traffic.
EFA map handles are entry addresses; lookup/removal validate them, while ordinary data-transfer address lookup only checks removed entries in strict mode.
EFA raw endpoint identity includes raw address bytes, QPN, and QKey rather than device identity or application rank alone.
The reverse AV key interleaves sixteen-bit AHN and QPN fields using portable spreading or optional BMI2 PDEP.
Direct AV insertion/removal test checks first table index zero, QPN/QKey preservation, successful lookup, removal, and failed lookup afterward.
EFA duplicate-address tests distinguish equal full addresses from equal GID with different QPN/QKey, while map tests assert pointer representation and strict-mode removal checks.
FI_EP_MSG uses listening/event-driven connection requests, creates an endpoint from FI_CONNREQ information, and connects or accepts before outbound transfers.
Tag matching masks ignored bits on both values; source restriction applies only to configured directed-receive endpoints.
Directed-receive functional coverage explicitly selects efa and parameterizes message/tagged operations, three sizes, memory types, and completion semantics.
Multi-receive can produce several message events and a final buffer-release event even when other successful completions are suppressed.
Direct/datagram injection requires FI_CONTEXT2; absent mode gives zero inject size and unsupported inject calls, unlike protocol-based efa RDM injection.
RMA read passes peer handle, remote address, remote key, local descriptor, and context as distinct arguments to the endpoint operation.
Write, fetch, and compare atomic validity dispatch to distinct callbacks with datatype, operation, and supported count.
Atomic test handlers validate each operation/datatype family before posting, optionally verify payload correctness, and treat unsupported combinations separately.
Direct read/readv fixtures condition RMA support on device features, otherwise assert EOPNOTSUPP; supported 4 KiB paths assert one mocked submitted work request.
EFA does not advertise FI_RMA_EVENT target events and documents target-side initiator AV insertion for direct and homogeneous-peer RMA.
FI_MR_VIRT_ADDR, PROV_KEY, RAW, ENDPOINT, LOCAL, and HMEM specify independent address, key, association, and local-registration responsibilities.
FI_MR_ALLOCATED requires mapping stability; when absent, the provider must update supported live registrations for coordinated mapping changes, with possible MMU notification duties.

The internal cache-hit fixture acquires the same host range twice, asserts the same cache entry, closes one reference per acquisition, and only then frees the allocation; returned references can alias one embedded MR.
Registration validation tests assert EINVAL/no MR for excess IOVs and ENOSYS/no MR for an uninitialized CUDA interface.
HMEM setup checks interface bounds and negotiated FI_HMEM initialization; its compatibility branch assumes system memory when FI_HMEM is absent.
RDM deregistration bumps generation before base deregistration; cache-backed close instead drops an entry reference through ofi_mr_cache_delete.
Generation capture preserves the initial snapshot on repost, and generation validation applies to TX operations rather than RX operations.
Generation tests verify slot reuse increments generation, repost does not replace its captured snapshot, and closing the MR makes the queued TX generation check fail.
Interface initialization is separate from device P2P support, and protocol thresholds can use system-memory behavior when direct access is unavailable.
Disabled-P2P CUDA test keeps interface initialization true, sets direct-support false, and makes unintended CUDA allocation probing fail the fixture.
CUDA getinfo support is inferred from instance-type data without creating a CUDA context; missing instance data assumes P2P support instead of proving registration.
Instance-type fixtures assert known unsupported, known supported, and missing-type assumption branches without allocation/context probes.
P2P REQUIRED rejects absent/disabled device support; PREFERRED/ENABLED reject global disable; DISABLED is accepted only for CUDA with API at least 1.18.
CQ positive counts, EAGAIN, EAVAIL/readerr, entry formats, and transmit/delivery/target-visibility semantics remain separate contracts.
Zero-count CQ read fixture posts the initial internal receive pool, leaves no pending or held packets, and clears the endpoint-scan flag.
RDM CQ progress posts initial receives, polls device CQs, and progresses queued peers/operations with distinct lock scopes; wait support depends on SHM configuration.
Injected send/receive device errors yield EAVAIL and readerr entries with nonzero portable error, expected provider errno, and nonempty diagnostics.
EFA domain identity distinguishes RDM/direct/datagram, retains device/PD/MR pool and accounting, and selects no-op versus mutex data-progress locks by threading model.
Direct/datagram domain close rejects live external child resources with EBUSY while accounting separately for its internal bounce-buffer registration.
Fabric-name dispatch selects direct base fabric or the RDM fabric rather than applying one resource/data path to every EFA entry.
RDM endpoint owns protocol packet pools, unexpected/reorder storage, peer maps, queued operations, backoff state, and progress-list membership.
RDM peers are endpoint-specific; map cache/peer-map fast paths precede lazy peer construction under the control lock.
AV entry teardown removes per-endpoint cached peers and maps before freeing provider entry resources; this does not authorize application use after removal.
Generic send resolves peers, checks backoff and TX packet capacity, allocates a TX entry, and returns EINVAL/EAGAIN at those admission gates.
Normal current protocol order is eager, medium, runtread, longread, then longcts; effective endpoint and operation flags are applied before predicates.
Selector may fill missing descriptors once for MR-seeking candidates and releases temporary selection registrations before a no-selection legacy fallback.
A recognized force-protocol name bypasses ordinary eligibility predicates; unknown names fall back, while SynapseAI has a separate longread branch.
Legacy selector tries recognized override, eligible read family, eager, medium, then longcts; old runtread choice maps to longread and posting checks handshake/extra peer features.
Eager capacity subtracts actual request-header size from MTU, constructs one packet with callback, and leaves TX/message-ID cleanup to its caller on construction failure.
Medium requests MR preparation, checks interface-specific medium threshold, and reports non-delivery completion only after all payload bytes are acknowledged.
Normal longread eligibility requires P2P, every IOV descriptor, interface minimum read size, and peer read interoperability.
Runtread adds no-delivery-complete, no read message already in flight, and positive peer runt-allowance gates to read eligibility.
Ordinary eager send completion finishes the operation; delivery-complete eager waits for receipt and the shared release predicate while packet release is separate.
Receipt/EOR processing validates live TX IDs, reports the required public completion, and retains TX state until local and remote release conditions are satisfied.
Tagged RTM processing invokes matched protocol callbacks or saves the callback and queues unmatched tagged work for a future receive.
Small and zero-length selection tests choose eager; simulated ordinary send completion changes one live TX operation to zero.
Failed-post regression injects device post failure, asserts a nonzero send result, restores peer next_msg_id exactly once, and leaves zero live TX operations.
Repeated RNR test preserves retransmit flags across repost, adds backoff on the second RNR, rejects repost with EAGAIN during backoff, and resets state on completion.
Forced longread CUDA functional test gates RDMA/HMEM/CUDA/inter-node support, controls protocol/runt settings, moves finalize traffic out of band, and checks read bytes and work-request counters.
Current EFA cache-entry registration asserts system memory and documents implicit registrations only; it must not be generalized to caching every public explicit/device MR.
